correctness.rationale: Geometric fixed points are exactly orbit-barycenters when supports are unions of vertex orbits: exact PL identification, not vertexwise fixed subcomplex. For n>=6 every face has at most four original vertices because five vertices force an independent triple; admissible 4-subsets have a two-edge perfect matching. Rotation order>=3 supports no orbit; order2 halfturn gives cycle C_{n/2}. Odd reflections have singleton plus paired orbits yielding C_{(n+1)/2}; even vertex-axis C_{n/2+1}, edge-axis C_{n/2}. n=3..5 K is a full simplex, so all element fixed sets contractible. I independently enumerated all orbit-face complexes for n=3..14 and all dihedral elements; they matched the exact f-vectors and classes. Inspected source verify_dihedral_fixed.py checks n<=35. Unlimited claim rests on orbit/matching proof, not the samples.
